implementation_notes: CompletableDeferred<T> is waiter and completer in one thread-safe object, so the correlation table is a ConcurrentHashMap of deferreds and the reply path is a single complete call; the deadline comes from withTimeout inside the calling coroutine, which cancels the await and lets a finally block remove the entry. kotlinx.coroutines is a library rather than part of the Kotlin stdlib, so nothing here is absorbed into the language - but with it present no hand-written signalling or listener registration is needed. On the JVM the reply usually arrives on a library's own thread, which is safe because the CompletableDeferred contract guarantees thread-safe completion from concurrent coroutines.
pitfalls: CompletableDeferred.complete returns false when the deferred is already completed or cancelled - that is the expected late-reply case, not an error, so do not throw on it.
The entry must be removed even when the coroutine is cancelled (hence the finally block); otherwise every cancelled call leaks a deferred together with its continuation.
Never call suspending functions inside ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent or while holding a lock: the mapping function is not a coroutine context and long work there blocks every caller of the map.
Completing from a non-coroutine thread is allowed, but resuming UI work on the wrong dispatcher requires an explicit withContext(Dispatchers.Main) at the consumer.
